newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong meat re-exports topped $2 bln - attache.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong meat re-exports topped $2 bln - attache.

text.p: Hong Kong's re-exports of live animals, meats and related products in 1996 totaled more than one million tonnes valued at more than $2.0 billion, according to a U.S. agricultural attache report made public Friday.

The June 13 report, prepared by an attache with the U.S. embassy in China, said that Hong Kong re-export data often is better tool in analyzing China's import situation than China's official trade data.

"The border between China and Hong Kong is quite porous, leading to substantial import under-counting by Chinese customs officials," the report said. "For many products, Hong Kong re-exports are higher than Chinese imports as indicated by their official statistics. In order to avoid paying full tariff rates, many importers under-invoice, mislabel, or mix their cargos with lower tariff products."

In 1996, re-exports originating from the United States equaled 548,184 metric tons worth $619 million, the report said. Meats, raw hides and skins overall registered the highest numbers, with chicken parts the biggest item and the United States the leading supplier.
Chicken feet and wings were the biggest re-exports, totaling $215 million and $169 million, respectively. The percentages from the United States were 79 percent and 55 percent, the report said.
